chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) ruled in the case of a woman whom her brother married to a man, then after that her mother, her uncle, and a younger brother married her to another. She was entered by the second husband and became pregnant. They disputed over her. The first husband presented witnesses, so he attached her to himself (maintained the first marriage) and gave her both dowries. He prevented the husband who had the right to enter her (the second one) until she gave birth to her pregnancy, then he attached the child to its father. The ruling in this report is what we said in the first report: that the girl gave her affair to her two brothers, and the older brother preceded with the contract, so his contract is valid and the contract made by the younger brother is void. In any case, if the second one entered her, she is entitled to the dowry for what he made lawful of her private part, and the child is attached to him, because he contracted with her and did not know that his older brother had already contracted her to another before that, and it was a contract of doubt (shubha), so the child is attached to him.
ai.seo_question: How is paternity and dowry determined when a woman is married multiple times by her guardians in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In *Al-Istibsar*, Shaykh al-Tusi records Imam Ali’s (AS) nuanced ruling on marital contracts where multiple guardians (brothers, mother, uncle) marry the same woman, establishing that the first valid contract prevails while subsequent unions are treated as 'contracts of doubt' (*'aqd al-shubha*). This classification ensures that if a later husband consummates the marriage in good faith, unaware of the prior contract, the child is attributed to him, reflecting the Shia principle of preserving lineage through equitable legal presumptions.
